claims.text: Combining DSC with CALPHAD modeling will accurately and efficiently determine melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, and entropy of fusion across the HEA family.
The combined approach will determine volume change at melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the HEA family.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi and Al0.5CoCrFeNi can be treated as single-phase solid solutions with high configurational entropy in the proposed initial state.
Low-temperature heat capacity can be extrapolated toward 0 K using the Debye T3 law, and DSC can be continued to incipient melting.
A calibrated, optimized DSC heating rate minimizes overlapping transitions and resolves latent and sensible heat contributions.
CALPHAD assessments can combine binary and ternary interaction data with configurational mixing contributions.
An inert atmosphere and uniform sample preparation avoid secondary-phase precipitation during the measurements.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a distorted yet uniform HEA solid solution.
High configurational entropy causes a pronounced and reproducible heat-capacity jump at melting.
The heat-capacity jump facilitates lever-rule and integration methods for resolving fusion parameters.
CALPHAD modeling separates configurational and vibrational thermodynamic contributions.
DSC directly provides cp(T) and identifies latent heat through a sharp signal near the solidus.
Integration of DSC heat-capacity and latent-heat data yields enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
CALPHAD databases based on binary and preferably ternary interactions predict temperature-dependent Gibbs-energy changes.
Configurational entropy of mixing lowers melting temperature and reduces the driving force for crystallization.
Fusion enthalpy, entropy, melting temperature, and volume change will be obtained within approximately ±10–20% of conventional reference methods.
The approach applies broadly to multicomponent alloys lacking pronounced secondary-phase segregation.
Traditional DSC without CALPHAD integration or explicit configurational entropy is less precise and less generalizable for HEA fusion properties.
Performance degrades for alloys with more than five principal elements, substantial precipitation, or sparse binary and ternary thermodynamic data.
Incomplete thermodynamic databases and overlapping phase transitions create uncertainty in combined DSC–CALPHAD predictions for HEAs.
